beats.beat: The company operates in two segments: infrastructure creation (railways, bridges, roads) and a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant at Thane.
Contracts are won through a competitive bidding process where the lowest quote typically wins, followed by a letter of acceptance and performance guarantee deposit.
Major clients include government entities: Western Railway, Central Railway, MCGM, MMRDA, and others; Western Railway alone contributed 52% of the order book.
Revenue is heavily concentrated: top customers accounted for 57% of total revenue in FY2018.
The company cites competitive strengths such as long-standing client relationships (since 2006 with Western Railway), modern techniques like box pushing, and a healthy order book.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations has declined from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a decrease of about 33%.
Net profit after adjustments fell from ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, then surged to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit before interest, depreciation, and tax) fluctuated: ₹784.46 lakhs (FY2014), ₹945.78 (FY2015), ₹783.31 (FY2016), ₹676.19 (FY2017), ₹928.80 (FY2018).
Total assets rose from ₹7,062.34 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹8,232.15 lakhs in FY2018.
Total borrowings (long-term + short-term) increased from ₹3,668.90 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹3,670.44 lakhs in FY2018, with short-term borrowings rising steadily.
The company has reported negative cash flows in recent years, a risk factor highlighted in the DRHP.

beats.beat: Sole promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra holds 74,95,476 equity shares, representing 90.949% of pre-issue capital.
Key management: CFO Anchal Pachori (CA), Company Secretary Mohit Soni (ACS). Hatim Sakerwala holds 9% equity shares as KMP.
Related party transactions include loans from KMP/Board of ₹68.4 lakhs and director remuneration of ₹57.7 lakhs in FY2018; outstanding payables to related parties stood at ₹324.3 lakhs.
No directors are on the RBI willful defaulter list, and no criminal cases have been filed against directors. However, two promoter group companies were struck off by ROC for non-operation.

beats.beat: The Indian construction sector is highly fragmented, working-capital intensive, and contributes about 8% to India's GDP.
Market size was estimated at US$ 400 billion in 2015, projected to reach US$ 1,000 billion by 2025, with FDI in construction development at US$ 24.67 billion (April 2000 – December 2017).
Growth is driven by government initiatives like 100 Smart Cities, AMRUT, Make in India, rising urbanization, and eased FDI norms.
The filing acknowledges headwinds: slow pace of government projects, working capital crunches, and changes in government policies.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited is a Mumbai-based infrastructure contractor focused on railway, bridge, and road construction, also operating a ready-mix concrete plant.
The company is seeking a listing on the SME Board of BSE/NSE via a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each at a price to be determined.
Proceeds will be used primarily for working capital (₹1,130 lakhs) and general corporate purposes, with the company's sole promoter holding 90.9% pre-issue.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: who the company is, what it does, what it is raising and why it matters.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each; the issue price will be determined later. There is no offer for sale component.
The lead manager is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited; the registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.
Proceeds: ₹1,130 lakhs for working capital requirements; the amount for general corporate purposes is not disclosed.
The face value is ₹10 per share; the issue price multiple over face value has not been fixed.

beats.beat: Extreme client concentration: Indian Railways (Western Railway primarily) contributed 57% of FY2018 revenue. Loss of this customer would severely impact revenues.
Revenue dependence on government tender awards: failure to win bids or acceptance of lower bid values could materially affect performance.
Negative cash flows in recent years and high working capital requirements pose liquidity risks, especially given short-term borrowings of ₹3,537.35 lakhs (FY2018).
The company has issued equity shares at prices lower than the issue price within the last 12 months, potentially diluting earlier investors.
Two promoter-group companies were struck off by the ROC for non-operation, indicating past governance issues.
